blocks.html: A queue is a linear data structure in which items are added at one end, called the rear (or back), and removed from the other end, called the front. The item that comes first is served first. This rule is called FIFO: First In, First Out.

lessons.title: 4.3 Implementing a queue with an array

blocks.html: In Python, a list with append() and pop(0) can act as a queue. In C++ we first build one ourselves to understand how it works, and then use the library version.
We use an array and two indexes: front (the index of the first item) and rear (the index of the last item). At the start, front = 0 and rear = -1 .

blocks.text: 4.3.2 The problem with a linear queue

blocks.html: Try this with MAX = 5 :

blocks.code:
LinearQueue q;
for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) q.enqueue(i * 10);   // 10 20 30 40 50
q.dequeue(); q.dequeue(); q.dequeue();            // 10, 20, 30 leave
q.enqueue(60);                                    // Queue Overflow!

blocks.html: Only 2 items are left and 3 slots are empty, yet the queue reports overflow. The reason is that rear has reached the last index (4) and can only move forward. The slots freed at the beginning (index 0, 1 and 2) can never be used again. This wasted space is the main weakness of a linear queue.
The fix is to join the end of the array back to the start, like a ring. When rear reaches the last index, it wraps around to index 0 if that slot is free. The modulus operator does the wrapping:

blocks.code:
rear  = (rear + 1) % MAX;     // 4 -> 0 when MAX = 5
front = (front + 1) % MAX;

blocks.html: We also keep a count of items, which makes it easy to tell "empty" from "full".
In step 4, rear wraps from 4 to (4 + 1) % 5 = 0 and reuses the free slot. The linear queue could not do this.

items.html: A queue is a linear data structure. Items are added at the rear and removed from the front, following FIFO (First In, First Out).
Operations: enqueue (add at the rear), dequeue (remove from the front), peek/front, isEmpty, isFull and size.
Overflow: enqueue on a full queue. Underflow: dequeue on an empty queue.
A linear queue in an array cannot reuse slots freed at the front, so it may report overflow while slots are still empty.
A circular queue wraps the indexes with (index + 1) % MAX and reuses every slot. Keeping a count makes the empty and full checks simple.
